papers.title: One Electrifying Decade of Organic Syntheses: A Literature Survey Based on Different Electrode Combinations
papers.abstract: Synthetic organic chemistry offers an endless scope in various domains of science, and electro-organic synthesis has grown as a green alternative to synthetic organic chemistry, obviating the necessity for harmful oxidants and reductants. Electro-organic reactions have attracted considerable attention globally in both academia and industry. This study analyzes the electrochemical organic synthesis towards the synthesis of valuable organic compounds. Electro-organic methodologies encompass C—P/C—O/C—N/N—N bond formation, C—H/N—H functionalization, C—N/C—S cross—coupling, ring expansion, oxidation dearomatization/annulation, C—H thiolation, dehydrogenative C(sp2)—H amination, C(sp3)—H/C(sp2)—H functionalization, sulfur insertion, Henry reaction, and Buchwald–Hartwig amination. This review emphasizes the synthesis of diversified organic compounds that possess remarkable biological features and show considerable potential in medicinal chemistry. The current review summarizes the reports from the recent decade that represent electro-organic synthesis for the development of diversified organic compounds.

papers.title: Beyond a solvent: HFIP as a game-changing medium in heterocyclic ring construction
papers.abstract: 1,1,1,3,3,3-Hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP) has emerged as one of the most powerful and versatile solvents in modern organic synthesis owing to its exceptional hydrogen-bond-donating ability, low nucleophilicity, high ionizing power, and remarkable capacity to stabilize ionic and radical intermediates. These unique physicochemical properties enable HFIP to facilitate proton transfer, activate otherwise unreactive bonds, and promote a wide range of intermolecular interactions, making it highly valuable in heterocycle synthesis. Over the past decade, the application of HFIP has expanded significantly, particularly in C–H functionalization and heterocyclic ring construction, where it frequently acts not only as a solvent but also as a promoter, cocatalyst, and reaction-directing medium. In this review, we comprehensively and critically summarize the latest representative advances in HFIP-enabled heterocyclic ring formation reported from 2022 to 2025. Particular emphasis is placed on mechanistic understanding, synthetic efficiency, substrate scope, and the multifunctional role of HFIP in controlling chemo-, regio-, and stereoselectivity. HFIP-mediated transformations often proceed under mild, metal-free, oxidant-free, or redox-neutral conditions and enable challenging cyclizations, annulations, dearomatizations, rearrangements, and cross-dehydrogenative coupling reactions that are difficult to achieve using conventional solvents. Mechanistic discussions throughout the review highlight the ability of HFIP to stabilize cationic, radical, and transition-state intermediates through extensive hydrogen-bonding networks and cooperative interactions with catalysts or reagents. For clarity, the review is organized according to the structural classes of the target heterocycles and the nature of the synthetic strategies employed. The review focuses on the construction of simple five-membered heterocycles; fused heterocyclic systems, including five–six- and six–six-fused frameworks and polycyclic fused architectures; spiro heterocycles, including five–five- and five–six-spiro systems generated through radical, ionic, electrochemical, and dearomative cascade processes; and saturated and non-aromatic heterocycles, encompassing three-, five-, six-, seven-, and nine-membered rings, mixed five-/six-membered frameworks, and polyfused saturated systems. Overall, this review demonstrates that HFIP has evolved far beyond a conventional fluorinated solvent and now serves as a powerful reaction-enabling platform in modern heterocyclic chemistry. By critically comparing recent methodologies and mechanistic paradigms, this review aims to provide a unified perspective on the expanding role of HFIP and inspire future developments in sustainable heterocycle synthesis.

papers.title: Alkyl-BODIPYs as a Self-Photoredox Catalyst for their Oxidative Hydroxymethylation
papers.abstract: The adoption of photocatalytic approaches for utilising small organic molecules in self‑catalysed reactions offers opportunities in green organic synthesis. We report that alkylated boron‑dipyrromethenes (BODIPYs) act as self‑photoredox catalysts for their own oxidation under mild visible‑light conditions. Using an imidazolinium salt (NHC-H) as a quencher, alkylated BODIPYs are oxidised cleanly to the corresponding hydroxymethyl derivatives in a one‑pot process. Luminescence studies, including Stern–Volmer analysis, support a reductive‑quenching pathway in which the NHC-H transfers an electron to photoexcited BODIPY to give a BODIPY radical anion. The method proceeds without external photocatalysts or stoichiometric oxidants and shows good functional‑group tolerance, highlighting the potential of these chromophores both as substrates and catalytic light absorbers. Moreover, the synthesized molecules were demonstrated to behave as effective passivating agents for layered Mn2+

papers.title: Tuning the mechanical integrity and corrosion performance of open-cell copper foams: identification of an optimization threshold
papers.abstract: Abstract In this work, Porous copper foam samples were fabricated by a space-holder technique with water-atomized copper powder and sodium chloride (NaCl) particles in weight fractions ranging from 10 to 35 wt%. The powders were mechanically mixed at a 10:1 ball-to-powder ratio and 150 rpm for 2 h. The effects of space-holder content on the physical, mechanical, tribological, and electrochemical performance were systematically investigated. Increasing the NaCl fraction precisely controlled the total porosity, from 39.15% to 57.76%, and reduced the bulk density from 5.452 to 3.785 g/cm³. XRD and SEM analyses confirmed a single-phase FCC copper matrix and a structural transition from isolated pores to a highly interconnected open-cell network. Consequently, Vickers hardness, compressive yield strength, energy absorption capacity decreased from 52.12 to 29.23 HV, 18.25 to 1.65 MPa, and 35.73 to 10.46 MJ/m³, respectively, following a modified Gibson–Ashby model (R 2 = 0.95). Concurrently, the coefficient of friction and specific wear rate increased (reaching a maximum of 0.73 mm³/N·m under 15 N for 35 wt% NaCl) due to strut thinning and localized delamination. Electrochemical evaluation in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution revealed an optimization threshold for sample fabricated with 25 wt% NaCl, which exhibited the lowest corrosion rate of 0.918 mm/y, and the highest polarization resistance (Rp) of 267.28 Ω, due to a stable Cu 2 O passive film. Exceeding this threshold at 30 and 35 wt% NaCl led to structural instability and stagnant electrolyte zones, accelerating corrosion kinetics. Overall, lower-porosity porous copper foam architectures offer superior structural energy absorption, whereas the 25 wt% NaCl configuration achieves an optimal balance between mechanical integrity and corrosion resistance.

papers.title: Skeletal Editing of Cycloparaphenylenes by Direct Oxygen Insertion
papers.abstract: Direct modification of the carbon framework of cycloparaphenylenes (CPPs) remains challenging despite the substantial strain stored in these carbon nanorings. Here, we report two complementary chemical methods for inserting an oxygen atom into a C–C bond of pristine [n]CPPs and the methylene-bridged [6]CPP ([6]MCPP) to give the corresponding oxylene derivatives. Treatment with m-chloroperbenzoic acid and copper(II) acetylacetonate affords mono-oxygenated products from [6]–[9]CPP in modest yields. Photocatalytically generated singlet oxygen is more efficient for smaller, more strained nanorings: [6]MCPP is converted to [6]MCPP-oxylene in 58% yield within 0.5 h, whereas the reactivity decreases sharply with increasing CPP size. Density functional theory calculations reveal that oxygen-insertion enthalpies become progressively less exothermic with increasing ring size and correlate linearly with 1/n, providing a thermodynamic context for the observed ring-size dependence. X-ray crystallography and strain analysis further reveal that oxygen insertion redistributes strain across the ring and lowers molecular symmetry. The resulting CPPoxylenes show markedly altered photophysical properties, with [9]CPP-oxylene reaching ΦF = 0.91. Prolonged photocatalysis of [6]MCPP enables a second, regioselective oxygen insertion at the most highly strained remaining C–C bond of the mono-oxylene framework. The resulting dioxylene adopts a more elongated structure and emits blue fluorescence at 414 nm with ΦF = 0.39; timeresolved measurements show that the higher fluorescence efficiency arises primarily from suppression of nonradiative decay. These results establish direct oxygen insertion as a route to skeletal editing of CPPs and connect sequential editing with changes in strain distribution, molecular geometry, and photophysical behavior.

papers.title: Beyond Wittig: Phosphonium Ylides and Salts as Catalysts and Precursors in Radical Chemistry
papers.abstract: Phosphonium ylides are classically recognized as nucleophilic reagents for carbonyl olefination. However, recent studies have revealed that their reactivity extends well beyond conventional two‐electron processes. They serve as catalysts in radical reactions and as sources of carbon‐centered radicals under thermal or photochemical activation. We give particular attention to the mechanistic distinctions among direct P─C bond homolysis, photoinduced single‐electron transfer (SET), and ylide radical‐cation‐mediated hydrogen‐atom transfer (HAT). Structurally related phosphonium salts are discussed separately as complementary radical precursors that undergo single‐electron activation and selective P─C bond fragmentation to generate carbon‐ or phosphorus‐centered radicals. The review also evaluates the experimental evidence used to support these mechanisms and identifies current limitations in substrate scope and catalytic efficiency. Future opportunities in catalyst design, asymmetric synthesis, electrochemical activation, and flow photochemistry are also outlined. These developments broaden the established reactivity profile of organophosphorus compounds and provide a foundation for more general and predictive single‐electron transformations.

papers.title: Selective Electroreductive N ‐Alkylation of Nitroarenes
papers.abstract: Aryl amines are privileged structural motifs ubiquitous in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and natural products. Herein, we report an electrocatalytic reductive coupling of nitroarenes with alkyl halides that enables the direct and step‐economic synthesis of N ‐alkylarylamines. This protocol features mild electrochemical conditions, broad functional group tolerance, and an exceptionally wide substrate scope, accommodating both benzylic and aliphatic halides. The synthetic utility of this method is further underscored by gram‐scale synthesis and a series of downstream derivatizations, highlighting its practicality and sustainability.

papers.title: Theoretical Insights Into the Molecular Mechanism of Fe Catalysed Sonogashira Cross‐Coupling Reaction
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The Sonogashira type cross‐coupling reaction constitutes a pivotal method for constructing C(sp)–C(sp) bonds, enabling the synthesis of structurally diverse aryl alkynes with broad applications in pharmaceuticals and materials science. In the present study, a comprehensive mechanistic investigation of the iron‐catalysed Sonogashira‐type coupling between phenylacetylene and 4‐iodoacetophenone was performed employing density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The catalytic system, comprising FeCl6HO and 1,10‐phenanthroline in aqueous medium under aerobic conditions, was examined in detail. Our results elucidate a mechanistic pathway that proceeds via an initial formation of the pre‐catalytic species through an interaction between the metal iron and the ligand phenanthroline, followed by base‐assisted activation of the terminal alkyne to form the active catalytic species, culminating in C–C bond formation through a concerted nucleophilic substitution process. This study reveals a feasible redox‐neutral mechanistic pathway where the iron centre remains in its +3 oxidation state throughout the reaction cycle and thereby provides valuable insights into the reactivity of the iron‐catalysed Sonogashira coupling reaction.

papers.title: Organic Electroreductive Transformations
papers.abstract: Comprehensive Summary As a green and efficient organic synthesis strategy, electrochemical reduction reactions have become an important method for constructing carbon‐carbon and carbon‐heteroatom bonds, owing to their unique advantages, including electrons serving as clean reducing agents, mild reaction conditions, controllable and adjustable potential, and favorable atom economy. They exhibit broad application prospects in fields such as the total synthesis of natural products, the preparation of pharmaceutical intermediates, and the synthesis of functional materials. Compared with traditional thermochemical reduction reactions, electrochemically driven reduction reactions can achieve selective regulation of reaction pathways by precisely controlling the electrode potential, thereby effectively avoiding side reactions, environmental pollution, and product separation difficulties caused by external reducing agents. Meanwhile, it can activate inert chemical bonds and accomplish transformations that are challenging to realize via traditional methods. This review systematically summarizes the recent research progress in electrochemical reduction reactions. Classified by substrate types, it elaborates on the reaction mechanisms, catalytic system design, and reaction selectivity regulation strategies of electrochemical reduction reactions involving different substrates. Additionally, the current challenges and future development directions in this field are prospected, providing a reference for the development and application of novel electrochemical reduction reactions. papers.title: Triple Atom Transfer-Enabled α-C(sp3)-H Aminomethylation of Aliphatic Amines: General and Modular Access to Vicinal Diamines
papers.abstract: Vicinal diamines are prevalent structural elements in organic molecules. In particular, those featuring a tertiary alkylamine motif are commonly found in biologically active molecules and therapeutic agents. However, methods for the efficient construction of these architectures from inexpensive and readily available feedstocks remain scarce. Here, we report a mild photocatalytic protocol for the modular synthesis of vicinal alkyl diamines via triple atom transfer-enabled α-C(sp3)–H aminomethylation. This transformation integrates halogen-atom transfer (XAT) and intramolecular 1,5-hydrogen-atom transfer (HAT) processes to furnish key α-amido alkyl radicals, which subsequently add to in situ-generated iminium ions. Critical to the success of the reaction is the cooperative action of a nickel complex and a zinc salt, which jointly promote the aminomethylation process. Utility of this method is demonstrated through late-stage modification of complex amine molecules, scale-up experiments, and ready access to scaffold-diverse free vicinal diamines. In addition, compatibility with aromatic aldehydes and the ability to functionalize alternative C–H sites further expand the chemical space of diamine architectures, highlighting the robustness and synthetic versatility of this protocol.

papers.title: Chromoselective Control for Aminoalkylation of CF3‑Alkenes through Low-Energy Photoredox Catalysis
papers.abstract: Recent advances in chromoselective photoredox catalysis have demonstrated that light wavelength can serve as a powerful and orthogonal reaction parameter, enabling divergent reactivity from a single catalytic system. Building on recent advances in the sequential decarboxylative/defluorinative aminoalkylation of trifluoromethyl-substituted alkenes, we report a divergent, wavelength-dependent strategy for the site-selective functionalization of N-arylglycines. High-throughput experimentation (HTE) was used to systematically screen photocatalysts and irradiation wavelengths to identify the most suitable divergent conditions. Interestingly, using [Ru(bpy)3]2+ as photocatalyst, irradiation with blue light promotes efficient difunctionalization of CF3-alkenes with N-arylglycines, affording monofluoroalkenyl-1,5-diamines, while switching the irradiation to red light enables selective monofunctionalization, delivering the corresponding gem-difluoroalkenyl amine intermediates exclusively under otherwise identical conditions, via a spin-forbidden transition pathway. This wavelength-governed switchable reactivity provides a powerful and tunable platform for the controlled radical modification of amino acids, expanding the synthetic utility of visible-light photoredox catalysis in divergent amine synthesis. Mechanistic investigations using photoelectrochemistry and TD-DFT have revealed notably a photo-excitation of intermediates, allowing for the second functionalization to whether happens or not, based on the irradiation wavelength used.

papers.title: Development of a Screening Workflow for the Halogenation of Nitrogen Heterocycles with Vanadium-Dependent Haloperoxidases
papers.abstract: Abstract The halogenation of nitrogen heterocycles is a privileged transformation for accessing important synthetic intermediates and biologically active targets in medicinal chemistry. Despite the importance of N-heterocycle halogenation, current methods rely on reagents or catalysts that are largely unselective and produce a significant number of waste products. With an emerging interest in using halogenating enzymes to address these challenges, the vanadium-dependent haloperoxidase class of enzymes has emerged as a powerful platform for halogenation reactions under a uniquely broad set of reaction conditions. Herein, we report the development of a screening workflow for the halogenation of heterocycles with chloroperoxidase from Curvularia inaequalis (CiVCPO). Using a high-throughput screening strategy, representative model heterocycles are screened for direct chlorination and bromination reactions, and the optimized conditions are translated to an extended substrate scope in moderate to high yields. The volume of high-throughput data obtained allowed for the development of a predictive model for the substrate halogenation conditions. This screening platform is applied to established industrial intermediates and to the discovery of previously undiscovered enzymatic nitrogen-chlorine bond formation and decarboxylative halogenation reactions.

papers.title: Tunable Aza-BODIPY Photocatalysts for Near-Infrared Metallaphotoredox Atom Transfer Radical Polymerization
papers.abstract: The merger of photoredox and transition-metal catalysis has significantly advanced radical and redox transformations, yet its reliance on UV or visible light continues to limit applications in optically complex and spatially confined environments. Herein, we introduce a modular family of tetraaryl aza-boron-dipyrromethene (aza-BODIPY) organic photocatalysts (PCs) for near-infrared (NIR) metallaphotoredox atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP). We systematically modulated peripheral electronics and core bromination, evaluating the dyes through quantum-chemical, electrochemical, and spectroscopic methods. This approach identified the key parameters governing catalytic performance: a delicate interplay between triplet-state accessibility, redox properties, and photostability. The optimized aza-BODIPY dye enables well-controlled ATRP of diverse acrylates and methacrylates at ultralow catalyst loadings, down to 5 ppm PC and 50 ppm copper complex. The system is further translated to open-air aqueous conditions, enabling rapid, high-throughput synthesis of water-soluble polymers in a 96-well plate format. Taking advantage of the enhanced penetration of NIR light, we demonstrate controlled polymerization through challenging physical barriers, including ex vivo tissue. Overall, this work defines design principles for far-red/NIR-absorbing aza-BODIPY PCs and expands the scope of NIR-mediated polymer synthesis to optically turbid, spatially restricted, and aqueous environments.

papers.title: Photochemical Aminomethylation of C(sp 3 )–H Bonds via Hydrogen Atom Transfer
papers.abstract: Direct installation of an aminomethyl group onto aliphatic C–H bonds provides an attractive route to valuable amine-containing building blocks but remains challenging with conventional polar approaches. Here, we report a photochemical aminomethylation of C(sp3)–H bonds enabled by hydrogen atom transfer (HAT). Photoexcited benzophenone directly abstracts hydrogen from αamino, α-oxy, and α-thio C–H bonds, generating carbon-centered radicals that are intercepted by an in situ-formed N-protected formimine. This strategy provides direct access to protected vicinal diamines, amino alcohol derivatives, and related aminomethylated products without requiring prefunctionalization of the C–H donor. Notably, the C–H substrate can be employed as the limiting reagent, while selective radical generation suppresses overfunctionalization. Translation to continuous flow reduces reaction times from 20 h to 3 h, while improving yields for the investigated substrates, and enables scalable synthesis. Subsequent deprotection and functionalization further demonstrate the synthetic utility of the resulting aminomethylated products.

papers.title: Direct Synthesis of α‐Amino Ketones From Aldehydes and Amines via Photocatalytic In Situ Imines Hydroacylation
papers.abstract: α‐Amino ketones have essential applications in pharmaceuticals and organic synthesis. The hydroacylation of imines is an attractive approach to access such valuable compounds. However, existing methods for hydroacylation with readily available aldehydes are highly dependent on the prepreparation of imines. Here, we report a photocatalytic protocol for synthesizing α‐amino ketones directly from aldehydes and amines. This one‐pot reaction proceeds smoothly in the presence of the photocatalyst tetrabutylammonium decatungstate (TBADT) and catalytic amounts of HBr. Aldehydes serve as both precursors for in situ imine formation and subsequent acylating agents. Hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) photocatalysis exhibits excellent two‐stage compatibility, allowing the transformation under mild and simple conditions. This strategy avoids the prepreparation and isolation of imines, providing an atom‐ and step‐economical route for the convenient synthesis of α‐amino ketones.

papers.title: Enantioconvergent Decarboxylative Cross-Coupling for the Synthesis of α-Aryl Ketones via Metallaphotoredox Catalysis
papers.abstract: Abstract Photochemical enantioselective nickel catalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for constructing stereogenic C(sp3)–C(sp2) bonds in organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry. Herein, we report a photoredox/nickel-catalyzed enantioconvergent decarboxylative cross-coupling of α-aryl carboxylic acid derivatives with aliphatic carboxylic acids, providing efficient access to enantioenriched α-aryl ketones. The reaction selectively engages two structurally distinct carboxylic acid-derived coupling partners while suppressing competing protodecarboxylation and homocoupling pathways. This protocol features broad substrate scope, good functional group tolerance, and excellent enantioselectivity (up to 98% ee), providing a modular and practical approach to chiral α-aryl ketones from readily accessible carboxylic acid feedstocks.

papers.title: A photoinduced, FeX3-catalyzed, stereo- and regio-selective halofunctionalization of olefins with MXn via a radical-polar crossover reaction
papers.abstract: The classical reaction for the halofunctionalization of olefins involves hazardous and highly toxic molecular halogens. The goal of chemists is to establish green, inherently safe, highly efficient and sustainable synthetic methods. Here, we report a green approach for the halofunctionalization of alkenes with MXn and FeX3, as well as a nucleophile at room temperature under visible-light irradiation in AcOH/CH3CN, without strong oxidants and any ligand. This procedure provides a wide substrate scope and excellent functional-group tolerance, ranging from alkenes and conjugated dienes to medicinally active fragments. The reaction results in good to excellent yields, such as 82% and 84% for the bromoalcoholization and chlorobromination of cyclohexene, respectively. The method exhibits high stereoselectivity, regioselectivity and chemoselectivity, and mechanistic studies support the hypothesis that the reaction is a cascade process based on radical-polar crossover species, supported by DFT calculations. The classical reaction for the halofunctionalization of olefins involves hazardous and highly toxic molecular halogens. Here, the authors report the FeX3-catalyzed halofunctionalization of alkenes with MXn at room temperature, under visible-light irradiation, and without strong oxidants.

papers.title: Modular Construction of Cyclic and Linear Quaternary Carbon Centers through Visible‐Light‐Induced Triplet Nitrene Transfer Reaction
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT All‐carbon quaternary centers represent a fundamental structural unit found in a wide range of functional molecules. Within the versatile synthetic toolbox, the semipinacol rearrangement (SPR) stands as one of the most powerful tools for assembling this sterically congested motif. In this context, ‌radical‐mediated SPR pathways‌, especially those entailing alkyl migrations, remain underexplored from a strategic standpoint. Herein, we report a visible light‐promoted formal SPR of tertiary allyl alcohols using in situ‐generated triplet nitrene species as the initiator under redox‐neutral conditions. This method demonstrates broad substrate scope, enabling efficient construction of all‐carbon quaternary centers across various steric environments, including rigid cyclic/spiro frameworks and flexible acyclic systems. Mechanistic investigations reveal substrate‐dependent pathways: alkenyl cyclobutanols undergo triplet nitrene addition followed by concurrent ring‐expansion and hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) to form cyclic ketones, while nonactivated allyl alcohols proceed through aziridination/ring‐opening/SPR sequences to produce linear β‐amino ketones. Preliminary biological assessments of these α‐quaternary β‐aminoketone derivatives revealed that compound 4a exhibited potent anti‐DENV‐2 activity, with an EC 50 value of 0.95 ± 0.02 µM against viral replication.

papers.title: Visible-Light-Mediated Decarboxylative Coupling of Aromatic Carboxylic Acids with Aryl Methyl Ketones to Unsymmetrical 1,2-Diketones
papers.abstract: A transition-metal-free and operationally simple strategy has been developed for the synthesis of unsymmetrical 1,2-diketones via a visible-light-induced decarboxylative arylation–oxidation cascade. Readily available aromatic carboxylic acids serve as convenient aryl precursors, and Eosin Y acts as an inexpensive organic photocatalyst. Under mild blue-light irradiation (450 nm) at room temperature in PEG-400 and in the presence of air as the oxidant, a broad range of unsymmetrical 1,2-diketones is obtained in good to excellent yields with good functional-group tolerance. Control experiments confirmed the essential roles of light, Eosin Y, and molecular oxygen, and TEMPO inhibition was consistent with a radical pathway. The protocol avoids precious-metal catalysts and stoichiometric oxidants, providing an efficient and practical route to valuable 1,2-diketone scaffolds from abundant starting materials.

papers.title: Photocluster catalytic oxidation enabled by structurally precise copper-hydride nanoclusters
papers.abstract: The utilization of light energy emerges as a prominent strategy to boost nanocluster catalysis, spurring rapid growth in the field termed photocluster catalysis. In particular, structurally well-defined copper-hydride nanoclusters attract attention as promising photocluster catalysts for organic synthesis. Herein, we report Cu13H6 exhibits excellent activity for photocatalytic α-C–H oxidation, revealing great potential in oxidation chemistry. Cu13H6 is one-pot synthesized and characterized using advanced analytical techniques. Critically, machine learning tentatively identifies hydride positions, reducing dependence on neutron diffraction. The Cu13H6 nanocluster exhibits outstanding activity in the photooxidation of diverse alkyl aromatics and alcohols to ketones under mild conditions. This pathway also supports photocatalytic defluorination, deuteriation, cyclopropane ring-opening and dehydrogenative coupling. This work tentatively determines the structure of Cu13H6 using robust stochastic surface walking global optimization with neural network, and identifies the cluster as a versatile, efficient photocatalyst that broadens photocatalysis applications in organic synthesis. The utilization of light energy has emerged as a prominent strategy to boost copper nanocluster photocatalysis for organic synthesis, but the scope of transformations remains relatively narrow. Here we report the catalytic performance of a copper-hydride nanocluster, Cu13H6, for photocatalytic α-C–H oxidation.

papers.title: Modular synthesis of 3,3-diaryloxetanes
papers.abstract: Abstract Oxetanes are strained four-membered oxygen heterocycles that are valuable motifs for modulating lipophilicity, metabolic stability and three-dimensional structure of pharmaceuticals. Diaryloxetanes with 3,3-substitution are recognized as bioisosteres of diaryl ketones that preserve key electronic features while exhibiting distinct reactivity. However, synthesis of this motif largely relies on Lewis acid-promoted Friedel–Crafts reactions, which are restricted to electron-rich arenes and often suffer from low functional-group tolerance and competing side reactions. Here we report a method for the synthesis of 3,3-substituted diaryloxetanes from readily available 3-oxetanone through a cross-coupling reaction with tetrafluoropyridone as leaving group. The difunctionalization through subsequent addition of two aryl groups, one from an aryl halide, the other from an arylboronic ester, provides access to a variety of benzophenone bioisosteres. The nickel-catalysed cross-coupling at a fully substituted carbon centre is enabled through oxetanyl C–O bond oxidative addition and establishes programmable entry to 3,3-diaryloxetane bioisosteres that are synthetically challenging to access via traditional polar bond disconnection strategies. Mechanistic studies support a Ni(0)-mediated oxidative addition of the oxetanyl tetrafluoropyridine ester.

papers.title: Modular Cyano-fluoroalkylation of Unactivated Alkenes Enabled by Photoinduced Fe-LMCT Catalysis
papers.abstract: Abstract We describe the implementation of an iron catalyzed cyano-fluoroalkylation of unactivated alkenes that leverages inexpensive trifluoroacetic acid (CF3CO2H) and related carboxylic acids (CFnRCO2H) as radical fluoroalkyl sources, together with tosyl cyanide (TsCN) as a low-toxicity cyanation reagent. Notably, the mild and redox-neutral conditions of the method are compatible with a broad range of substrates, including alkenes containing biologically relevant motifs (40 examples, up to 83% yield). The resulting β-fluoroalkylated nitriles can be diversely derivatized to afford other valuable fluorinated sp3-rich architectures. Mechanistic studies have revealed the key role of a protonated bipyridine-based ligand in enhancing reaction efficiency.

papers.title: Carbon Quaternization at the α-Position of Thiazoles: Iron-Catalyzed Hydroheteroarylation Using Unactivated Alkenes
papers.abstract: Abstract Thiazoles are privileged N-heterocyclic scaffolds ubiquitous in FDA-approved drugs, yet their clinical utility can be compromised by oxidative metabolism at the heterobenzylic position. Inspired by the metabolic-blocking strategy used in dabrafenib development, herein we report an iron-catalyzed strategy for direct α-quaternization of (benzo)thiazoles using unactivated alkenes. Under the proposed pathway, alkene-derived carbon-centered radicals undergo regioselective C2 addition and oxidative rearomatization, providing α-quaternary products without heteroarene preactivation or stoichiometric Lewis acids, thereby enabling analogue diversification.

papers.title: μ-Oxo-Bridged Iodine(III) Reagents Enable Catalyst- and Light-Free Fluoro(halo)methyl Radical Generation
papers.abstract: While conventional radical fluoroalkylation typically requires exogenous catalysts or photoactivation to overcome significant kinetic barriers, here we report bench-stable μ-oxo-bridged iodine(III) reagents that release fluoro(halo)methyl radicals upon heating without an external catalyst, additive, or light. The resulting radicals initiate cascade cyclizations of methacrylamides and methacrylohydrazides to afford fluorinated oxindoles, pyrazolones, and related heterocycles. Variation of the fluorinated carboxylate ligand within the iodine(III) reagent framework controls the identity of the transferred C1 fragment, thereby providing chlorofluoromethyl, bromofluoromethyl, difluoromethyl, and monofluoromethyl products from a common reagent architecture. The transformation is compatible with structurally diverse and natural-product-derived substrates and proceeds efficiently upon scale-up. By encoding the required bond lability directly into the iodine(III) framework, this strategy establishes a general platform for the catalyst-, additive-, and light-free generation and incorporation of fluorinated C1 radicals into complex molecular frameworks.

papers.title: Photocatalyst‐Free Hydrodifluoromethylation of Alkenes via Thiol‐Mediated Photoactivation of Zn(CF 2 H) 2 (DMPU) 2
papers.abstract: Herein, we report a photocatalyst‐free hydrodifluoromethylation of alkenes using Zn(CF 2 H) 2 (DMPU) 2 and thiophenols under 390 nm irradiation. The thiophenol serves a dual stoichiometric function, promoting the formation of a photoactive thiol‐modified organozinc species while acting as the terminal hydrogen‐atom donor. The reaction is applicable to styrenes, electron‐rich and electron‐deficient alkenes, and 1,1‐disubstituted alkenes, as well as selected internal and unactivated aliphatic alkenes. Its synthetic utility is further demonstrated by the late‐stage difluoromethylation of biologically relevant molecules. Preliminary mechanistic investigations, including radical‐clock experiments, spectroscopic analysis, and 19 F NMR experiments, support a radical pathway involving thiophenol‐induced speciation and photoactivation of the organozinc reagent, followed by hydrogen‐atom transfer to the resulting carbon‐centered radical. These findings establish thiophenol‐mediated photoactivation as a distinct strategy for exploiting Zn(CF 2 H) 2 (DMPU) 2 in radical difluoromethylation.

papers.title: Wireless Bipolar Electrochemistry for Organic Electrosynthesis: Principles, Mechanistic Insights, and Emerging Autonomous Systems
papers.abstract: Wireless bipolar electrochemistry (BPE) has emerged as a powerful platform for organic electrosynthesis, enabling redox transformations on electrically floating conductors without direct electrical wiring. Through electric-field-induced polarization, bipolar electrodes simultaneously promote spatially separated oxidation and reduction reactions, offering unique opportunities for reaction design, miniaturized reactor architectures, parallel processing, and sustainable chemical synthesis. Recent years have witnessed significant advances in both exogenous and endogenous bipolar electrochemical systems, expanding the scope of wireless electrosynthesis to asymmetric transformations, flow chemistry, low-electrolyte conditions, autonomous microreactors, and self-propelled electrochemical systems. This review critically examines the fundamental principles governing bipolar electrochemistry, recent developments in organic synthesis, and emerging diagnostic methodologies, including split bipolar electrodes and electrochemiluminescence-based imaging, which have substantially improved mechanistic understanding of charge transport, polarization phenomena, and reaction control. The advantages and limitations of wireless bipolar systems are evaluated in comparison with conventional electrolysis, highlighting challenges associated with reaction selectivity, scalability, energy efficiency, and quantitative electrochemical characterization. Finally, future opportunities involving advanced materials, operando analytical techniques, artificial intelligence-assisted optimization, and continuous-flow processing are discussed. Collectively, these developments position wireless bipolar electrochemistry as a promising enabling technology for next-generation sustainable electrosynthesis and autonomous electrochemical manufacturing.

papers.title: Difluoromethylenation of Alkynes: Streamlined Access to Allyl Difluorides
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT A direct difluoromethylenation of alkynes has been developed using HF/pyridine as a dual acidic and fluorinating medium. The reaction proceeds via in situ generation of a primary oxocarbenium ion from formaldehyde, enabling efficient formation of two C(sp 3 )─F bonds and one C(sp 2 )═C(sp 2 ) bond in a single step without the need for pre‐functionalized reagents. This strategy offers a concise route to allyl difluorides as a complementary approach to incorporate difluoromethylene motifs into complex molecular frameworks. Additional spectroscopic and computational investigations provide insights into this mechanism.

papers.title: Synthesis and In Vivo Incorporation of 4‐Difluoromethyl‐L‐Phenylalanine Into Proteins
papers.abstract: The difluoromethyl group exhibits unique chemical and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopic properties. Here, the synthesis and characterization of 4‐difluoromethyl‐L‐phenylalanine is reported. Methods have been developed to incorporate this versatile unnatural amino acid into full‐length green fluorescent protein and carbonic anhydrase, using an orthogonal transfer RNA (tRNA)/synthetase pair with standard genetic code expansion techniques. Taking advantage of the characteristic 19 F NMR behavior of the difluoromethyl group, the potential application of the difluoromethyl group as a probe in protein NMR studies was explored.

papers.title: Iron-Catalyzed Defluorinative Alkylation for Accessing Cyclic Acetal– gem -Difluoroalkenes
papers.abstract: Abstract Cyclic acetals and gem-difluoroalkenes are proven structural motifs in medicinal chemistry, yet their modular incorporation into a densely functionalized hybrid architecture remains an uncharted frontier. Herein, we disclose an Fe-catalyzed reductive defluorinative cross-coupling between trifluoromethyl alkenes and 1,3-dioxolanyl- or 1,3-dioxepanyl-substituted alkyl iodides, enabling the rapid assembly of five- or seven-membered cyclic acetal-embodied fluorinated scaffolds, respectively. This protocol enriches defluorinative coupling versatility and offers streamlined access to structurally diverse pharmaceutically relevant scaffolds.
